protocol_extensions.label: G4push
protocol_extensions.instruction: Push the mouthpiece 5 mm further onto the cork, play G4 mf, then put it back.

sensitivity.about: d feature / d control (per control unit) at the default player, per test note; raw v1 features

robust_transform.about: See docs/COACHING.md 'Robust transform v1'. Implemented in tools/coach/common.py robust_vector().

definitions.cents@L: cents of note L (absolute, vs target × regime)
definitions.X_rel@L: feature X of mf note L minus the mean of X over all mf notes (X = H2..H6, tilt, odd_even, edge, hnr): removes the recording's EQ/room colouring
definitions.scoop@L: scoop of mf note L (low weight)
definitions.X_mean: mean over mf notes of X (tilt, odd_even, edge, hnr, centroid_rel) — absolute, colour-sensitive (low weight)
definitions.X_ff-pp@G4 / X_mf-pp@G4: dynamic deltas on G4 (level, centroid_rel, tilt, H2..H4, edge)
definitions.cents_push-ref@G4: cents(G4 with mouthpiece +5 mm) − cents(G4) (protocol extension G4push)

room_notes.too_reverberant: The recording is too reverberant for tone-colour analysis: only pitch-based advice (tuning, stability, register) is given. Record closer to the bell or in a drier room.
room_notes.some: Some room sound detected: harmonic-shape evidence is down-weighted.
room_notes.uncertain: Room could not be estimated; using average robustness weights.

weights.about: w_i = 1/σ_i, σ_i = RMS error of the robust feature under 32 room×mic×level colourings (floored); by_room: σ per room class of the blind room estimate (dry RT60 ≤ 0.25 s, some ≤ 0.7 s, too_reverberant: non-pitch features weight 0)

objective.definition: r = W·(robust(sim(u)) − robust(rec)) ⊕ λ·u, u = (control − default)/step over fit_controls

rules.cause: Mouthpiece too far out on the cork
rules.evidence: All notes flat by a similar amount (cents offset roughly uniform across both registers); tone otherwise normal.
rules.advice: Push the mouthpiece further onto the cork — about 1 mm per 2-3 cents flat (more in the upper register). Re-check with a tuner on G4 and C6.
rules.why: The mouthpiece position changes the length of the whole air column: every note moves together. Pushing in 1 mm raises pitch by ~1.4 cents on low Bb and ~3.3 cents on C#5.
rules.listen_for: With a drone or tuner the whole instrument sits low, low notes and high notes alike.

rules.cause: Mouthpiece too far in on the cork
rules.evidence: All notes sharp by a similar amount.
rules.advice: Pull the mouthpiece out a little — about 1 mm per 2-3 cents sharp. Do not 'lip down' to compensate.
rules.why: A shorter air column raises every note by roughly the same proportion.
rules.listen_for: Everything sits high on the tuner, and relaxing the lip does not fix the low notes.

rules.cause: Biting / too much lip pressure
rules.evidence: Upper register and palm-key notes increasingly sharp, a thinner, pinched sound; ff does not open up.
rules.advice: Relax the jaw and let the lower lip cushion the reed instead of pushing it; think 'drop the jaw, keep the corners firm'. Re-tune after relaxing.
rules.why: Lip force pre-bends the reed toward the lay: the reed becomes stiffer (the lip tissue stiffens as you press) and its opening smaller, which raises pitch most on short tubes and limits the flow.
rules.listen_for: Pitch rising as you go up the horn, high notes thin and 'tight'; when you relax, the pitch drops and the sound gets bigger.

rules.cause: Embouchure too loose (not enough lip support)
rules.evidence: Upper notes flat and spread; low notes may honk; pitch unstable.
rules.advice: Firm the lip a little (corners in, chin flat) so the reed is supported; keep the air steady.
rules.why: Too little lip force leaves the reed very compliant and wide open: the reed's 'equivalent volume' grows, lowering high notes most.
rules.listen_for: High notes sagging flat and wide, the sound spreading at forte.

rules.cause: Too much mouthpiece in the mouth
rules.evidence: Notes flat (more in the upper register), loud and spread; low notes may crack to the octave.
rules.advice: Take a little less mouthpiece: place the lower lip about where the reed starts to leave the mouthpiece rail (mark it with a pencil line).
rules.why: The lip sits further from the reed tip, so the free vibrating reed is longer and softer: more reed compliance, lower pitch, less control.
rules.listen_for: A big but uncontrolled sound, flat and wobbly high notes.

rules.cause: Too little mouthpiece in the mouth
rules.evidence: Small, stuffy sound, low notes hard to start; slightly sharp.
rules.advice: Take a little more mouthpiece (a few millimetres) so the reed can vibrate freely.
rules.why: A short free reed is stiff: higher closing pressure, less flow, a smaller and darker sound.
rules.listen_for: Low notes refusing to speak softly, a pinched small tone.
gaps: In the simulator, moving the lip toward the tip raises the reed's closing pressure, the opposite of some real set-ups — treat as a hint.

rules.cause: Heavy lip cushion / damping (subtone-like)
rules.evidence: Dark, soft-edged sound with little 2-5 kHz energy at every dynamic; slightly flat.
rules.advice: Use a little less lower lip over the reed and less pressure from the lip tissue; let the reed ring.
rules.why: Lip tissue on the reed absorbs its vibration (damping), which removes upper partials and lowers the effective reed resonance.
rules.listen_for: A muffled tone that stays dark even when you play louder.

rules.cause: Too little lip cushion (thin lip, 'reed buzz')
rules.evidence: Edgy/buzzy tone with strong 2-5 kHz energy, especially loud.
rules.advice: Roll a little more of the lower lip over the teeth to cushion the reed.
rules.why: With little damping the reed's own resonance rings, adding high-frequency buzz.
rules.listen_for: A 'zzz' edge on every note.

rules.cause: Reed too hard for the set-up
rules.evidence: Stuffy, needs a lot of air; soft notes hard to start; dark; slightly sharp.
rules.advice: Try half a strength softer (or sand the reed slightly) and compare the low notes at pp.
rules.why: A stiffer reed raises the closing pressure, so more blowing pressure is needed before the reed sounds.
rules.listen_for: Effort and resistance; low notes cracking or not speaking softly.

rules.cause: Reed too soft
rules.evidence: Upper register flat, sound closes up or buzzes at ff, bright and thin.
rules.advice: Try half a strength harder.
rules.why: A soft reed closes easily: the pitch of high notes sags and loud notes choke.
rules.listen_for: High notes going flat as you crescendo; the sound 'shutting off' when you push.

rules.cause: Wide tip opening (jazz set-up) without the matching embouchure
rules.evidence: Loud and bright, wide intonation, low notes cracking; more air needed.
rules.advice: Either a closer facing / softer reed, or more lip support; check G4 pp holds pitch.
rules.why: A larger reed opening lets more air through: louder and brighter, but the reed is harder to control.
rules.listen_for: Big sound but unstable pitch, hard to play softly.

rules.cause: Bright mouthpiece (high baffle / small chamber)
rules.evidence: Bright, edgy tone across the range, more so than the embouchure explains; register 2 slightly sharp.
rules.advice: If you want a darker/classical sound: a lower-baffle, larger-chamber mouthpiece. Otherwise it is a style choice.
rules.why: A high baffle narrows the air path just behind the tip, which boosts upper partials.
rules.listen_for: A bright 'cutting' tone even at mf.
gaps: Baffle and chamber are partly confounded with each other in this test set (|corr| ≈ 0.65-0.73).

rules.cause: Large-chamber (dark) mouthpiece
rules.evidence: Dark tone; the upper register flat relative to the low register (octaves narrow).
rules.advice: Adjust with the cork for the middle of the horn, then voice the upper register up (tongue higher) — or use a smaller-chamber mouthpiece for better octaves.
rules.why: A larger mouthpiece volume replaces the cut-off tip of the cone less well at high frequencies: the second register goes flat relative to the first.
rules.listen_for: Octaves (G4–G5, D4–D5) that are narrow (top note flat).

rules.cause: Not enough air support
rules.evidence: Soft, thin sound at mf, little brightening from pp to ff, notes slow to start.
rules.advice: Breathe lower and keep a steady, faster air stream; practise long tones crescendo pp→ff.
rules.why: Blowing pressure sets how far above the oscillation threshold the reed works: too little gives a weak, unstable note.
rules.listen_for: Notes that fade or wobble at the end of a phrase; small dynamic range.

rules.cause: Over-blowing (too much pressure for the set-up)
rules.evidence: Loud and harsh at mf, low notes jumping up an octave, slight pitch drop.
rules.advice: Use less pressure and more air speed control; let the reed do the work.
rules.why: At high pressure the reed beats hard against the lay: a harsh spectrum and register jumps on the low notes.
rules.listen_for: Low Bb/C cracking to the octave, an edgy forte that you cannot soften.

rules.cause: Closed throat / jaw in the low register
rules.evidence: Low notes slightly sharp and pinched compared with the middle register.
rules.advice: Open the throat and drop the jaw for the low notes ('aw' or 'oh' vowel).
rules.why: The mouth cavity is in series with the horn at the reed; a smaller cavity slightly raises the pitch and thins the low notes.
rules.listen_for: Low notes thinner and higher than the middle register.
gaps: Weakly identifiable from the test set (the tract mainly matters in the upper register).

rules.cause: Low notes cracking to the octave (air/lip balance)
rules.evidence: regime ≠ 1 on Bb3 or D4 (sounds an octave or twelfth up).
rules.advice: Less pressure and a slightly looser lip for the low notes, more mouth cavity ('aw'); start them softly with a gentle tongue.
rules.why: For the lowest notes the 2nd air-column resonance is as strong as the 1st; too much pressure or lip force tips the reed into the upper regime.
rules.listen_for: The note popping up an octave as you push.

rules.cause: Unstable / sharp open C#5
rules.evidence: C#5 sharp by > 15 cents or pitch_std high relative to C5.
rules.advice: Relax the lip and voice lower on C#5; try adding the low C# key or RH fingers (standard alternate) to stabilise it.
rules.why: Open C# vents through a small hole with a very short tube: its resonances are weak and inharmonic.
rules.listen_for: A thin, wavering C#5.

rules.cause: Voicing set late (scooping into notes)
rules.evidence: Large |scoop| (> 25 cents) at the start of notes, mostly on palm-key / upper notes.
rules.advice: Set the tongue/throat shape before you start the note ('voice, then attack'), then release the tongue.
rules.why: The vocal tract is in series with the horn; if its shape changes during the attack the pitch slides.
rules.listen_for: A pitch 'swoop' at the start of high notes.
gaps: Attack/scoop features are unreliable in reverberant recordings; only trust with a close, dry recording.

rules.cause: Breathy / air leaking
rules.evidence: Low harmonic-to-noise ratio (hnr) on most notes relative to the other notes.
rules.advice: Seal the corners of the mouth around the mouthpiece; keep the air focused; check the reed for leaks.
rules.why: Air that does not pass the reed channel as a modulated jet adds broadband noise.
rules.listen_for: A 'hiss' under the tone.

rules.cause: Small dynamic range (pp too loud or ff too weak)
rules.evidence: G4 ff − pp level < 5 dB (the default simulated player gives ~7 dB on this protocol; real players typically 15-25 dB), little brightening.
rules.advice: For pp: more lip support and less mouthpiece pressure-air (firmer, smaller opening); for ff: more air with a looser, undamped lip.
rules.why: Dynamics on a reed instrument come mainly from the embouchure: the lip sets the reed's closing pressure, which scales the whole oscillation; pressure alone only changes the level by ~6-12 dB.
rules.listen_for: pp and ff sounding almost the same.
gaps: The simulator's pp intonation in register 2 is up to +40-60 cents sharp (A5, Bb5) — pp pitch advice is suppressed there.

rules.cause: Pinching at soft dynamics
rules.evidence: The pp note is more than 15 cents sharper than the same note at mf.
rules.advice: For soft notes keep the jaw relaxed and support the sound with air and lip corners rather than biting; drop the jaw slightly as you get softer.
rules.why: Playing softly with a firmer lip reduces the reed opening and stiffens the reed (strain-stiffening lip tissue): the pitch rises, most in the upper register.
rules.listen_for: Soft notes drifting sharp on a tuner, especially G5–C6.
gaps: The simulator's pp intonation in register 2 runs +40-60 cents sharp on A5/Bb5 — G4 is used for this check.

cause_ranking.about: PRIMARY (no fit needed): for each control rule, χ² improvement over the default player of the best magnitude template: score_r = χ²(y, default) − min_m χ²(y, T_r,m), χ² = Σ ((y_i − t_i)/σ_eff,i)², σ_eff² = σ_room² + σ_nuisance². SECONDARY (after a fit): projection of the fitted control change u/max(sd,0.3) on the rule signature. Observation rules fire from rule.trigger.

fit_based.about: LM fit + projection ranking; synthetic players = 1 fault (1.5-3 steps) + ±0.4-step nuisance; v1 protocol

template_v1.about: independent players: fault 1.5-3 steps + 0-0.75 step of a second cause + nuisance; random room/mic/level

template_G4push.about: independent players: fault 1.5-3 steps + 0-0.75 step of a second cause + nuisance; random room/mic/level
